rules: Import `ruststream_gcp_pubsub::prelude::*` at a mount site; a handler body imports `ruststream::prelude::*` and bounds its slot on a capability, except a body that writes an ordering key (Components: Prelude).

Read an existing subscription with bare `#[subscriber("orders-workers")]`; name settings on `GooglePubSub::new(name)`: `create_with_topic`, `max_outstanding`, `ack_extension`, `max_lease`, `batch_wait` (Components: Subscriptions, GooglePubSub).
Mount a manual `Handle` body with `subscriber(GooglePubSub::new("orders-workers"), Body)`, which takes the descriptor as the attribute does (Components: GooglePubSub).

Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(topic)` after `include`, both together and `n` in 5..=100; the pair becomes the subscription's own dead-letter policy, written at startup (Components: Dead letters).

Settle with the handler's outcome: `ack` acknowledges, `retry` nacks, `drop` acknowledges except on the last attempt of the subscription's dead-letter policy, where it nacks (Components: Acknowledgement).

`drop()` also follows a dead-letter policy set outside the code: the broker reads it once at startup, which needs `pubsub.subscriptions.get`; without it a warning is logged and the last-attempt drop acknowledges (Components: Acknowledgement).

Delay a redelivery with `HandlerOutcome::retry_after(delay)`: the delivery stays leased for the delay, then is nacked; size `GooglePubSub::max_lease` above the longest delay (Components: retry_after, max_lease).
Attach the publish policy under its prelude name: `.out(marker, Publish::default()).build()` for a slot and `.out_reply(Publish::default())` for a reply (Components: PubSubPublish).

Key one publish with `.ordering_key(..)` on the publish builder, the slot bounded `Out<impl Publisher<Options = PubSubPublishOptions>>`; key a mount site with `Publish::default().ordering_key(..)` (Components: ordering_key, Policy).

Read a delivery's ordering key with `message.partition_key()` or the `partition-key` header, and its attempt with `message.redelivery_count()`, sent only under a dead-letter policy (Components: PARTITION_KEY_HEADER, Attempts).
Take batches with a slice handler: `.batch(n)` at the mount site bounds their size and `batch_wait` on the descriptor the wait for a partial one (Components: Batches).

Run locally with `PubSubBroker::new(project).emulator(addr)`, `addr` a `host:port` or a URL; in production use Application Default Credentials, `credentials(..)` or a locational `endpoint(..)` (Components: emulator, credentials, endpoint).

Test a service by handing the app `main` runs to `TestApp::start`, which connects `PubSubBroker` in process with the `testing` feature, and address it as `tb.broker::<PubSubBroker>()` (Components: Testing).
Run the in-process test body against the emulator with `TestApp::start_live` for leases, flow control and ordered delivery; keep `TestApp::start` for the rest of the suite (Components: Live).
